conflicts.detail: RM Table92: CH0/CH7, intersecting exact inventory to CH0. Header: CH0/CH3 on both controllers. SVD exposes PFREQ on all four. CH0 is a common candidate, not full-domain resolution.
RM/header specify six bits; all eight SVD channel TR2 fields specify five. Do not truncate a future selector based on SVD width.
LL provides COMP2_OUT selector36 under exact COMP2 presence. RM Table94 ends at35; SVD five-bit field cannot encode36. SDK-only candidate, no admitted routing.
RM p432 TRIGSEL prose says active for TRIGPOL=00, contradicting its polarity table and pp388/414. Preserve this source defect.

contracts.detail: Request source, transfer address and trigger source are distinct. A peripheral request can support data/control/status transfers, but arbitrary endpoint pairings are not qualified.
SWREQ=1 ignores REQSEL, BREQ and PFREQ. GPIO IDR reads do not create a GPIO hardware-request selector.
LPTIM1_UE selector54 requires BREQ=1. I3C1_RX selector57 is listed for early termination; PFREQ channel conflict remains material.

Do not assign one physical hardware request to simultaneously active competing channels, including aliases/controller routes; no setting-error report is supplied. LPDMA2 SPI2S1_RX and SPI1_RX both encode4, not two endpoints.

Trigger fanout is permitted; one hit may pend, another can be lost with TOF without automatic channel disable. Fanout does not promise simultaneous sampling or completion order. Arbitration precedes the read, so GPIO state is not captured at the trigger edge.
No FIFO: one internally registered source-transfer cell. TR2 is read-only while enabled; configure only with EN=0/completed channel. Block/link/single trigger modes have distinct gating semantics.
DAC1_CH2 selector74 survives exact two-channel declaration; package naming/electrical conflict remains separate.
